_comment: Worked examples for the journey-times view (How long it really takes), grouped by area. Separate from journey_presets.json, which holds the Ticket view's campaign cases: these are everyday trips, chosen so that Brighton and Hove and Worthing are represented as well as the coast road between them. `from`/`to` are NaPTAN ATCO codes, checked against data/timetable.sqlite by pytest. At runtime a preset is shown only if a published service calls at both ends, so a stale one hides itself rather than leading to 'no journeys found'. Journey counts in `why` are from the published build of 23 September 2026 (seven days, 16 to 22 September).

presets.label: Brighton Station → Marina
presets.why: Across the city centre and along the seafront: the 7 (217 journeys, usually 24 min) and the 47 (86) both make it, so the service chips have a real comparison to offer.

presets.label: Churchill Square → County Hospital
presets.why: A hospital trip, where being late matters: the 1 (693 journeys, usually 12 min) and the 1X (445).

presets.label: City centre → University of Brighton
presets.why: The Lewes Road corridor students use: the 49 (456 journeys, usually 19 min) and the 25 (146).

presets.label: Churchill Square → Hove Town Hall
presets.why: Western Road into Hove, served by six services (1, 2, 5B, 6, 46, 49), each with 280 or more tracked journeys.

presets.label: Brighton Station → Hove Station
presets.why: Station to station: the 7 (732 journeys, usually 11 min) and the 3X (338). Also the pair that exposed the wrong-service bug, where the 3X opened with another service's stops.

presets.label: Preston Circus → Hollingbury Asda
presets.why: Up the hill to the Hollingbury shops on the 5B (197 journeys, usually 17 min).

presets.label: City centre → Whitehawk
presets.why: The 21 out to Whitehawk (326 journeys, usually 21 min), a route whose stop list was the most jumbled before stops were put in route order.

presets.label: Churchill Square → Portslade Station
presets.why: To the western edge of the city: the 1X, 6, 46 and 49 all make it, at noticeably different speeds.

presets.label: Worthing seafront → Durrington
presets.why: Across Worthing on the 700 (399 journeys, usually 17 min).

presets.label: Worthing Town Hall → Durrington
presets.why: A second way to Durrington: the 23 (98 journeys) and the 1 (79).

presets.label: Worthing → Findon
presets.why: Out to Findon on the 23 (30 journeys, usually 15 min): thinner evidence, which the view says beside the answer.

presets.label: Worthing → Lancing
presets.why: Along the coast road on the 700 (468 journeys, usually 9 min).

presets.label: Lancing → Shoreham
presets.why: The 700 between the two Adur towns (464 journeys, usually 11 min).

presets.label: Shoreham Station → Southlands Hospital
presets.why: A short hospital trip on the 2 (293 journeys, usually 8 min).

presets.label: Southwick → Brighton
presets.why: From Southwick into the city on the 46 (248 journeys).

presets.label: Shoreham → Brighton
presets.why: The clearest service comparison: the 700 usually takes 32 min and the 2 usually 58 (455 and 278 journeys).

presets.label: Worthing → Brighton
presets.why: End to end on the Coastliner 700 (106 journeys, usually 61 min).

presets.label: Lancing → Brighton
presets.why: The 700 from Lancing (106 journeys, usually 51 min), across the Worthing and Brighton fare boundary.

presets.label: Portslade → Brighton
presets.why: Four Brighton & Hove services from Portslade into the centre (6, 46, 49 and 25), a useful multi-service comparison.
